status: Prepared only: no tests, builds, imports, GPU operations, or execution validation were run by B12xCandidate.
operator: Main alone selects GPUs, stops/starts workloads, layers the running exact image, and executes validation.
installation: For each manifest.files entry, resolve its target under the installed Python package root and require its SHA256 to equal baseline_sha256 before copying the candidate source bytes. Do not layer onto a stale checkout or silently accept mismatches.

Copy only the two manifest.files source paths into their matching package-relative targets. Keep manifest.json and validation/ together at an isolated experiment location; they are not package modules.

Run from a neutral working directory without PYTHONPATH pointing at a checkout. Both scripts check the imported installed module's SHA256 against manifest.json before accessing CUDA; mismatches are fatal.

The scripts intentionally have no skip/fallback path for missing CUDA, mismatched candidate source, unsupported B12X runtime, failed collectives, or failed output checks. Preserve nonzero exits as failures.

commands.name: route_tail_cuda
checks: Actual CUDA route payload multiset, unique coverage, invalid-ID/expert-map rejection, per-expert block grouping, padded counts, live_numel route sentinels, -1 block sentinels, caller data pointers and guard suffixes.
PR226 small-prefix fixed arena max=24 rows, K1, E32, block=8 with tails 17/23/24; eager and captured execution, with and without expert maps.
PR226 prefill fixed arena max=1536 rows, K16, E896, block=8 with tails 1177/1184/1536; must return the full 30848 route-slot/3856 block-slot caller arena.
PR256 runtime-bound variation using another adequate max=1535 arena and differently aligned live tail lengths.
Preallocated expert-count path, allocation-based eager count path, and old captured-prefix fallback with explicit out-of-capture warmup.
Empty/below-bucket behavior and genuinely undersized arena ValueError remain intact.
commands.limits: No model weights. Finite cases, largest input 1536x16 int64 routes and roughly 31k int32 packed slots plus maps/counts/guard suffixes. CUDA contexts, JIT compilation and allocator reservation are additional; this is not a memory-margin benchmark.
commands.success: Exit 0, per-case JSON, and final JSON status=passed. No timing or no-recompile claim is made by this script.

commands.name: pcie_teardown_cuda
checks: Actual two-rank NCCL/PCIe eager reduction followed by transient-channel CUDA graph capture and three changed-input replays per cycle, with exact BF16 sums and no additional torch allocations during replay.
Destroy/reset graphs before releasing referenced IPC channels. Set each process current_device to the OTHER GPU before rollback and close.
All three real teardown barriers must explicitly target the pool owner's rank-local GPU; an unbound barrier raises before entering NCCL.
Rollback releases transient IPC ownership while preserving the retained channel, which must still perform a correct all-reduce.
Explicit close releases retained ownership; a repeated close is idempotent; current_device remains the unrelated GPU. Two complete cycles exercise re-creation.
commands.limits: Exactly two visible CUDA devices are required. Two processes, two cycles, at most two pool channels per cycle, max_input_bytes=65536 and 4x1024 BF16 input/output tensors; default rank-data storage is 8 MiB per channel. NCCL/context/compiler allocations are additional. No models or persistent weights. Internal 240-second worker deadline terminates and then kills surviving children; outer timeout is a second bound.
commands.success: Exit 0, each rank/cycle JSON confirming graph/rollback/reuse/close, and final JSON status=passed.
commands.caution: Do not wrap the whole rollback/close in torch.cuda.device(owner): that would mask the wrong-current-device condition. Existing status object collectives still use their baseline current-device policy; this exact runtime must be qualified rather than assuming upstream results transfer.

serving_followup: Only after source-hash checks and isolated CUDA correctness pass, Main can measure route-tail serving behavior and compilation events under the controlled experiment.
No throughput, prefill fairness, memory margin, numerical parity of a complete model, or global absence of serving-time compilation is established by this source layer or its unexecuted scripts.
PR256 intentionally leaves the small-prefix and legacy captured-prefix live scalar specialization unchanged. Existing alignment/bucket warmup remains relevant; do not remove it based on this patch.
